standard_prerequisites.name: Geometrically normal in codimension one: assumptions and consequences
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies geometric reducedness of A and normality of A' tensor_k K, which is what upgrades the inequality to an equality.

standard_prerequisites.name: The pre-delta construction
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the intermediate ring A' whose base change is compared on both sides.

core_obligations: Set A = O_{X,x} and B = O_{Y,y}; apply the geometrically-normal-in-codimension-1 criterion to see that A is geometrically reduced, so that B is a localization of A tensor_k K (proof lines 8535-8538).

Take A -> A' as in the pre-delta construction and use the same criterion to see that A' tensor_k K is normal, which is the extra input that is unavailable in the inequality version (proof lines 8539-8541).
Match the constructions on the two sides so that the lengths defining the two delta-invariants agree, and conclude the asserted equality (proof lines 8541-8561).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the two local rings as in the inequality version.
Obtain normality of the base change of the pre-delta ring from the criterion.
Compare the two length computations and conclude equality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma upgrades the comparison of delta-invariants across a base field extension from an inequality to an equality, assuming assumptions (a), (b), (c) of the geometrically-normal-in-codimension-1 criterion for x in X together with dim(O_{Y,y}) = 1. The proof again sets A and B equal to the two local rings and uses the criterion to get that A is geometrically reduced, hence B is a localization of A tensor_k K; the improvement over the inequality version is that A' tensor_k K is now normal by the same criterion, which lets the pre-delta construction be matched on both sides so that the two lengths agree (proof lines 8535-8561). H2: the use of normality of the base change of A' to make the comparison two-sided is the substance.
